motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast and mild for the season, 30°F, haze on the water thinner but slow to lift, a smell in the air Marigold calls 'lakewater on a stovetop'

undercurrent.phenomenon: an uncollected library card, due today, made out to nobody the town remembers, and now sixteen due-date stamps in sixteen different hands
undercurrent.note: Calloway's own inventory of the handwriting is the first time a resident has actively investigated rather than merely witnessed the phenomenon, which nudges the level up a notch. Agnes's refusal of Toby today is a deliberate held breath, not a retreat; it should pay off soon, possibly as her last riddle of the season, possibly delivered in writing again per her arc. Keep Russ's deflections sturdy but starting to sound rehearsed even to him. The 'warm to the touch' detail on the calendar cover is new and should recur or be confirmed/denied next time someone touches it. Do not let Gerald's not-writing calcify into a new ritual; give him one more small temptation to break it soon.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
